questions.explain: Silo = one database per tenant (max isolation, enterprise/compliance); pool = one database with tenant_id + RLS (cheapest, fastest onboarding — the book's default); bridge = pools for the tail, silos for the head (where most successful SaaS ends up).
options: Only the silo model is viable
Silo (per-tenant DB), pool (shared DB with tenant_id + RLS, the default), bridge (pools for tail, silos for head)
Pool, lake, and warehouse
Single-tenant only
questions.q: What are the three tenancy models and when does each fit?

questions.explain: tenant_id leads every composite index for partition-like elimination; very large pools can hash-partition the biggest tables by tenant; per-tenant filtered vector indexes are the vector equivalent of silo graduation.
options: Index by created_at first
tenant_id placement in indexes does not matter
One index per tenant
tenant_id leads every composite index; hash-partition large tables by tenant; per-tenant filtered vector indexes for the largest tenants
questions.q: How is the pooled model kept fast at scale?

questions.explain: Three mitigations in escalating order: Resource Governor workload groups (cap ingestion CPU, floor interactive), per-tenant ingestion throttles from the registry, and graduation to a silo for tenants exceeding their fair share.
options: Resource Governor caps, per-tenant ingestion throttles, and graduation to silos
Buy a bigger server immediately
Throttle all tenants equally
Ignore it; noisy neighbors are unavoidable
questions.q: How is the noisy-neighbor problem handled?

questions.explain: The quota check and decrement happen in a single atomic UPDATE…WHERE statement, so concurrent requests cannot overshoot the quota — @@ROWCOUNT = 0 means the quota is exceeded.
options: Read the quota, then update in a second statement
Application-level locking
A single atomic UPDATE…WHERE that checks and decrements together
Quotas are only advisory
questions.q: How is per-tenant token quota consumption made race-free?

questions.explain: Provision the silo with the same schema, backfill the tenant's rows, dual-write during a cutover window, verify row counts, flip the registry's deployment flag, then purge from the pool — no application changes needed.
options: Take downtime and move the data
Graduation requires rewriting the application
Provision silo → backfill → dual-write → verify → flip registry → purge from pool
Tenants can never leave the pool
questions.q: What is the zero-downtime tenant graduation path from pool to silo?
